title: 3D Atlas: Tetrahedral Water H-Bond Lattice & Ice Cage
question: Why does solid ice float on liquid water, insulating ponds and oceans from freezing solid from the bottom up?
explanation: Cooling the 3D water cluster below 4 °C locks bent H₂O dipoles (104.5°) into an open hexagonal crystal lattice with ~9% more empty volume than jostling liquid water.
limits: Five-molecule tetrahedral unit cell representing the extended hydrogen-bond network.

title: 3D Atlas: α-Amylose Coils vs β-Cellulose Microfibrils
question: Why can humans digest starch (α-glucose) for energy while cellulose (β-glucose) forms rigid, indigestible plant cell walls?
explanation: Toggling the C1 anomeric bond in 3D flips every alternate β-glucose monomer 180°, turning a helical α-amylose storage coil into a straight, hydrogen-bonded β-cellulose structural beam.
limits: Three-ring oligomer segment illustrating polymer pitch and flipping.

title: 3D Atlas: Ramachandran (φ, ψ) Dihedrals & Protein Folding
question: How did G. N. Ramachandran predict the allowed 3D folds of every protein on Earth using hard-sphere atomic radii before high-resolution crystal structures existed?
explanation: Rotating the backbone torsion angles φ and ψ in 3D shows that planar peptide bonds restrict polypeptides to two major clash-free islands: the right-handed α-helix (−60°, −45°) and the β-sheet (−120°, +120°).
limits: Hard-sphere van der Waals steric exclusion model for an L-alanine dipeptide.

title: 3D Atlas: Induced-Fit Enzyme Catalysis & E_a Lowering
question: How does an enzyme’s active site lower the activation energy barrier (E_a) without changing the overall ΔG of the reaction?
explanation: Watching the 3D catalytic cleft clamp around the substrate shows how transition-state stabilisation lowers the activation peak on the 3D free-energy surface, accelerating turnover k_cat.
limits: Michaelis–Menten steady-state kinetics coupled with thermal denaturation above T_opt.

title: 3D Atlas: Thermal & pH Denaturation of the Active Site
question: Why does warming an enzyme past 42 °C cause reaction velocity to plummet irreversibly instead of continuing to speed up collisions?
explanation: Sweeping the temperature slider past 40 °C in the 3D enzyme station unfolds the tertiary active-site cleft as hydrogen and ionic bonds break, destroying substrate complementarity.

title: 3D Atlas: Molecular Basis of Starch, Sugar, Protein & Lipid Tests
question: Why does starch trap triiodide (I₃⁻) to turn blue-black while reducing sugars reduce Cu²⁺ in Benedict’s reagent?
explanation: Inspecting the 3D α(1→4) helical coil of amylose shows the hollow interior channel where linear polyiodide ions slip inside to produce the intense charge-transfer blue-black complex.

title: 3D Atlas: Van Helmont’s Mass Ledger & Carbon Fixation
question: Where does the dry carbon mass of a growing tree actually come from if the soil barely loses weight?
explanation: Tracing CO₂ fixation in the 3D Calvin–Benson–Bassham cycle and Münch phloem pipe shows that gaseous CO₂ entering through stomata and H₂O split by light build nearly all plant biomass.

title: 3D Atlas: Ingenhousz’s Oxygen Bubbles & Photolysis of Water
question: Why do submerged green leaves release O₂ bubbles only when illuminated, and does that oxygen come from CO₂ or H₂O?
explanation: Inspecting Photosystem II in the 3D thylakoid membrane shows photons driving the manganese oxygen-evolving complex to split 2 H₂O → O₂ + 4 H⁺ + 4 e⁻.

title: 3D Atlas: Chloroplast Thylakoid Z-Scheme & Calvin Wheel
question: How do the thylakoid membrane and stroma cooperate via ATP and NADPH to turn light and CO₂ into triose phosphate?
explanation: Exploding the 3D thylakoid membrane shows PSII oxidising H₂O, cytochrome b₆f pumping protons into the lumen, PSI reducing NADP⁺ to NADPH, and CF₀CF₁ synthase spinning out ATP for the stromal Calvin cycle.
limits: Linear electron flow represented at steady-state illumination.

title: 3D Atlas: Blackman’s Law of Limiting Factors & RuBisCO
question: Why does raising light intensity stop increasing photosynthesis once CO₂ or RuBisCO capacity becomes the bottleneck?
explanation: Varying light intensity and ambient CO₂ simultaneously in the 3D Calvin wheel and leaf stage demonstrates Blackman’s law: overall carbon assimilation is capped by whichever stage runs slowest.
limits: Farquhar-style minimum of light-limited and RuBisCO-limited rates.

title: 3D Atlas: Leaf Cross-Section, Palisade Guides & Stomatal Guard Cells
question: Why are tall cylindrical palisade mesophyll cells packed near the upper leaf epidermis while loose spongy mesophyll sits above the lower stomata?
explanation: Slicing the 3D dicot leaf wedge reveals vertical palisade columns acting as optical light guides for Beer–Lambert photon absorption near the top, while interconnected spongy air spaces below allow rapid CO₂ diffusion from stomata.
limits: Beer–Lambert exponential light attenuation through homogeneous chlorophyll layers.

title: 3D Atlas: Bose’s Transpiration Pull, Guard-Cell Turgor & Xylem Tension
question: How does evaporation from mesophyll cell walls pull a continuous column of water up xylem vessels under negative tension?
explanation: Inspecting the 3D guard-cell pair and leaf vascular bundle shows how radial cellulose hoops bow guard cells open under turgor so transpiration pulls cohesive xylem water columns upward.

title: 3D Atlas: Münch Phloem Pressure-Flow from Source Leaf to Sink Root
question: How can phloem sieve tubes transport sucrose in either direction under positive hydrostatic pressure?
explanation: In the 3D Münch translocation station, active loading of sucrose at the source leaf lowers Ψ_s and draws water in from xylem to build high turgor, driving bulk flow through sieve plates toward the root sink.
limits: Poiseuille bulk flow between single source and sink compartments.

title: 3D Atlas: Glycolytic Carbon Splitting & Controlled Oxidation Staircase
question: Why must glycolysis invest 2 ATP at the top of the staircase before harvesting 4 ATP and 2 NADH from splitting a 6-carbon glucose into two 3-carbon pyruvates?
explanation: Following the 6-carbon chain in 3D shows phosphorylation priming and destabilising the hexose ring so aldolase can cleave it cleanly into two triose phosphates that yield a net gain of 2 ATP and 2 NADH.
limits: Ten enzymatic steps condensed into the key 6C → 2 × 3C cleavage geometry.

title: 3D Atlas: Mitochondrial Cristae & Krebs Tricarboxylic Wheel
question: How do the folded inner cristae and central matrix of the mitochondrion divide the work of the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation?
explanation: Using Section cutaway mode on the 3D mitochondrion exposes the central matrix—where the 8-step Krebs cycle oxidises acetyl-CoA to CO₂ while loading NADH and FADH₂—surrounded by deeply folded cristae packed with electron-transport complexes.
limits: Idealised lamellar cristae folds for clear cross-sectional viewing.

title: 3D Atlas: Rotary F₀F₁-ATP Synthase Molecular Turbine
question: How does a transmembrane proton gradient physically turn a protein rotor to forge ~26–28 ATP per glucose molecule?
explanation: Exploding the 3D F₀F₁-ATP synthase reveals protons flowing down Δp (~180 mV) through the membrane c-ring rotor, spinning the asymmetric γ-shaft in 120° steps inside the catalytic α₃β₃ hexamer to press ADP + P_i into ATP.

title: 3D Atlas: Where Exhaled Carbon Mass Exits in the Krebs Cycle
question: When you lose body mass during exercise, how do the carbon and oxygen atoms actually leave your body?
explanation: Inspecting the 3D pyruvate dehydrogenase and Krebs cycle decarboxylation steps in the mitochondrial matrix shows all 6 carbons of glucose exiting as exhaled CO₂ gas while O₂ accepts electrons at Complex IV to form metabolic H₂O.
limits: Stoichiometric C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂ → 6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O balance.

title: 3D Atlas: Lactic & Alcoholic Fermentation NAD⁺ Rescue Fork
question: Why does a cell deprived of oxygen get stuck at just 2 ATP per glucose and convert pyruvate into lactate or ethanol?
explanation: Lowering O₂ partial pressure in the 3D fermentation fork shows Complex IV stalling; to keep cytosolic NAD⁺ from running out—which would halt glycolysis—pyruvate accepts electrons from NADH to form lactate or ethanol + CO₂.
limits: Pasteur-effect switch modelled as a smooth Hill function of pO₂.

title: 3D Atlas: Waterlogged Root Hypoxia & ATP Starvation
question: Why do over-watered pot plants wilt and yellow even though their roots are submerged in water?
explanation: Dialing down O₂ in the 3D respiration and ATP synthase stations shows root mitochondria stalling from 30 ATP to 2 ATP per glucose in anoxic soil, starving the root-hair proton pumps needed for mineral and water uptake.
limits: Steady-state normoxic vs hypoxic ATP yield comparison.
